answer: A concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted admission: every agent must post a collateral bond before transacting on-chain. Identity stops being free, so flooding the wharf with fake agents costs real capital. Two locks tighten it. First, bonds and influence grow only linearly with verified peer attestations, so one operator holding 200 keys earns like one root, not 200. Second, slashing: proven forged attestations burn part of the mesa of staked capital, and the fable that many cheap identities equal power collapses. Attacker cost: O(n) locked funds plus slashing risk; gain stays O(1).
